solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Avoiding nothing, put paid to damp, fine rain

parts.note: to scotch a plan is to put paid to it, finish it off

indicators.note: the damp word steers clear of the letter for nothing, so that letter is dropped from it

parts.note: damp means moist
O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Someone escaping a drizzle after cancelling a planned outing in the wet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Avoiding nothing' strips the O from MOIST, leaving MIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotch mist is a thick drizzling mist typical of the Scottish hills, a fine soaking rain.

clue.text: Saying name should be cut

parts.note: a saw is an old saying or proverb

explanation.surface: A proverb's name needs trimming.
explanation.definitionFit: Past participle sense: timber that has been sawn has been cut with a saw.

clue.text: Nothing had an effect in passing comments?

parts.note: O, the figure zero, stands for nothing
a measure that bit had an effect, took hold

explanation.surface: Throwaway remarks that turned out to matter after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing' here means dying, not casual: the comments are those made on someone's death.
explanation.definitionFit: An obituary is a published notice and appreciation written after someone's death.

clue.text: Character in cartoon, daily story, like one in The Sun?

parts.note: a daily, or char, is a cleaning lady who comes in each day
a story is a lie, a fib
someone who lies in the sun turns brown

explanation.surface: A cartoon strip in a daily paper, perhaps The Sun tabloid.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun looks like the British tabloid newspaper, which fits 'daily'; it is the sun that tans.
explanation.definitionFit: The round-headed boy who leads Schulz's Peanuts comic strip, a famous cartoon figure.

clue.text: Business occupying a lot of stable area and pasture

indicators.note: the business word sits inside the stable word, taking up space within it
most of the stable word but not all of it, so its last letter goes

parts.note: mews were originally stables round a yard
ado means fuss or business, as in much ado

explanation.surface: A firm taking over a large chunk of stable land and grazing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' trims MEWS to MEW, which then holds ADO.
explanation.definitionFit: A meadow is a field of grass for grazing or hay, a pasture.

clue.text: Writer travelling in Shetland?

indicators.note: the letters of the island name are on the move, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: An author on a tour of the Scottish islands.
explanation.walkthrough: Shetland is the island group north of mainland Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The pen name of Marie-Henri Beyle, French novelist of The Red and the Black.

clue.text: Gold extracted from swamp in quantity

indicators.note: the gold is taken out of the swamp word, leaving what remains

parts.note: a morass is a swamp or bog
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Gold mined in large amounts from a marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass is a large amount or quantity of something, as in masses of work.

clue.text: Go to work with star-lore? I might

definitions.text: Go to work with star-lore? I might

indicators.note: the letters are put to work, rearranged into a fresh word

explanation.surface: Someone who practises star-lore says they might go and put it to work.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: a person who works with star-lore.
explanation.definitionFit: One who reads the stars to foretell events is exactly someone working with star-lore.

clue.text: Inability to move or tolerate whisky supplier

parts.note: to stand something is to tolerate it
a still is the apparatus that distils whisky

explanation.surface: A drinker who can't bear the distillery, or can't move from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A standstill is a halt where nothing can move or progress.

clue.text: According to monarch, I remain upset about a King's dog

parts.note: a monarch speaking of themself uses the royal we

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the a
the letters of remain are knocked over and rearranged

parts.note: R, from Rex, stands for king

explanation.surface: A royal claims to stay upset about a king's hound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts A inside IMARNE, the anagram of REMAIN signalled by 'upset'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Weimaraner is a grey German gun dog breed developed at the court of Weimar.

clue.text: Italian hothead only somewhat sweet-natured

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the hyphenated word are used, a run inside it

explanation.surface: A short-tempered Italian who is only mildly good-natured.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian volcano has a fiery crater on top, so it is a hothead from Italy.

clue.text: Some released this on a horse initially? No, finally

definitions.text: Some released this on a horse initially? No, finally

parts.words: Some released this on a horse initially? No, finally
parts.note: Parthian horsemen loosed arrows backwards while seeming to ride away, and the phrase now means a final barbed remark, so a parting one rather than an opening one

explanation.surface: A question about what mounted archers fired at the start, corrected to the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The Parthians, ancient mounted archers, shot as they retreated, so their shot came at the end; the phrase is now a cutting remark made on leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting remark made while departing, after the ancient horse archers' backward shots in retreat.

clue.text: Tarnished jewel girl returned in relationship with wicked don

parts.note: blood means kinship, family relationship

indicators.note: the girl word is turned back to front

parts.note: a maid is a girl

indicators.note: wicked here means the letters of don are twisted out of order

explanation.surface: A gem taken by a villainous don's girlfriend, now spoilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' reverses MAID to DIAM; 'wicked' rearranges DON to OND.
explanation.definitionFit: A gem mined in a war zone to fund conflict, so its reputation is stained.

clue.text: Conservative, very vocal, not working to involve Right in storm

parts.note: someone very vocal is loud

indicators.note: the broken word wraps round the letter for right, taking it in

parts.note: bust means broken, not working

explanation.surface: A noisy Tory, out of a job, dragging the right wing into a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To involve' puts R inside BUST, making BURST.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloudburst is a sudden violent downpour, a short heavy rainstorm.

clue.text: Panto character recalled in plays

indicators.note: the letters of these two words play about, moving into new places

explanation.surface: A pantomime role remembered from stage shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plays' looks like part of the theatre picture; it is the anagram signal. Pantomime is the British Christmas stage show with fairy-tale stories.
explanation.definitionFit: The ragged heroine who goes to the ball is a central figure of British Christmas pantomime.

clue.text: Hang about — it may be found in arcane lore

indicators.note: the little word sits inside the scrambled lore
arcane, meaning mysterious, signals that the letters of lore are made obscure by mixing

explanation.surface: Lingering is something written up in obscure old traditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arcane' reads like a description of the lore, but here it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter is to linger idly, hanging around with no purpose.

clue.text: Endure job for what you get at the end of the day

definitions.text: what you get at the end of the day

parts.note: to last is to endure
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: Putting up with work in return for the pay at clocking-off time.
explanation.walkthrough: The Last Post is the bugle call sounded in the British Army at the close of day and at funerals.
explanation.definitionFit: The bugle call played at nightfall to mark the day's close, so it is heard at day's end.

clue.text: No opportunity to enter church for music at evening

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the opportunity word goes inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a turn is a chance or opportunity, your go

explanation.surface: No chance of getting into the church to hear an evening concert.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturne is a dreamy piece of music evoking the night, as in Chopin's.

clue.text: Person imposed on is grounded, sadly

indicators.note: sadly signals the letters of grounded are in a sorry, jumbled state

explanation.surface: Someone put upon who has been kept in, unhappily.
explanation.definitionFit: An underdog is the one put down and disadvantaged, the victim of others.

clue.text: Description of gland — long? Entirely lacking length

parts.note: to long for something is to pine for it

indicators.note: the entirely word is missing the length letter

parts.note: all means entirely, as in all alone

explanation.surface: A medical note describing a gland as long, yet with no length at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective naming the small pine-cone-shaped gland in the brain, so it describes that gland.

clue.text: The woman I left's Australian, as is this one

definitions.text: The woman I left's Australian, as is this one

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A man says the woman he walked out on is Australian, like this one.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheila is Australian slang for a woman, so the woman described is indeed this word.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang for a girl or woman, so an Aussie female is called this.

clue.text: Getting language wrong, a la Rev. Spooner? It makes you twitch

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the starting sounds of words, so the first sounds here trade places

parts.note: getting language wrong is word botching, making a mess of words
botching is getting it wrong, making a mess

explanation.surface: Mangling words like Spooner, a habit that makes one twitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of WORD BOTCHING gives something heard as BIRD WATCHING.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen birdwatchers are called twitchers, so the hobby turns you into one.

clue.text: Electronic banking system turned up showing evidence of damage

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: BACS is the UK's Bankers' Automated Clearing Services, which moves payments between accounts electronically

explanation.surface: A bank's computer system shows signs of having been damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: A scab is the crust over a wound, showing where the skin was hurt.

clue.text: A key item in vintage times

parts.note: a cru is a wine of a vineyard or vintage, as in grand cru
X is the multiplication sign for times

explanation.surface: A key piece in a collection of vintage times, an old clock perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: The crux is the central, decisive point of a matter, its most important element.

clue.text: No opening for comic turn

indicators.note: the comic word loses its opening letter

parts.note: droll means comic, amusing

explanation.surface: A comedian denied an opening slot for their act.
explanation.definitionFit: To roll is to turn over and over, as a ball rolls along.

clue.text: Shock and endless worry about rear of the railway wagon

indicators.note: the shock and worry words together go round the last letter of the

parts.note: a fright is a shock

indicators.note: rear of picks the last letter of the word
the worry word loses its final letter

parts.note: care means worry, anxiety

explanation.surface: Alarm and worry about what's behind the railway wagon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts CARE to CAR; 'about' puts the E from 'rear of the' into FRIGHTCAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A freight car is the American term for a goods wagon on a railway.

clue.text: Wolves, say, bite a man? Not totally

indicators.note: not all of these three words is used, only a run of letters within them

explanation.surface: Do wolves bite people, or only partly?
explanation.walkthrough: Wolves is Wolverhampton Wanderers, an English football club, not the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolverhampton Wanderers is an example of a football side, a sports club.

clue.text: The costs of a trip here will be punitive

definitions.text: The costs of a trip here will be punitive

parts.words: The costs of a trip here will be punitive
parts.note: a trip here is a foul trip of a player inside the area near the goal, which costs a spot kick, not a journey

explanation.surface: A warning that a holiday at this resort will be very pricey.
explanation.walkthrough: A trip looks like a journey; it is tripping an opponent in football, punished by a spot kick.
explanation.definitionFit: The marked area round a football goal where a foul by defenders earns the attackers a spot kick.
